squawks.headline: Japan's PM Takaichi says the target pump price for petrol will rise by 5 yen per litre each month from December
squawks.detail: Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi said the target petrol price will go up by 5 yen per litre each month from December into the spring. She also confirmed the decision to subsidise power and gas bills from December.

squawks.headline: EU's Costa says the search for Lagarde's successor as ECB President begins today and will go ahead without delay
squawks.detail: European Council President Costa said Lagarde had told him she intends to leave the ECB presidency on 7 February 2027. He said the appointment process for her successor starts today.

squawks.headline: Japan's PM Takaichi says subsidies to curb electricity and gas bills will run from December to February
squawks.detail: Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi said the government will introduce support measures for household electricity and gas bills starting in December and running until February.

squawks.headline: Lagarde's successor at the ECB is to be appointed by the European Council under the EU treaty nomination process
squawks.detail: The European Council will appoint the next ECB President using the nomination procedure in Article 283 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. This follows Lagarde telling staff she plans to step down on 7 February.

squawks.headline: ECB President Lagarde tells staff she plans to step down on 7 February
squawks.detail: Reports on 29 October say ECB President Christine Lagarde has told staff she intends to leave her post on 7 February. The reports give no reason for her departure and name no successor.

squawks.headline: Haskel says ONS productivity revisions came too late for the OBR forecast; OBR raised total factor productivity for AI
squawks.detail: Speaking at a Resolution Foundation event, former MPC member Jonathan Haskel said recent ONS revisions that lift output per hour arrived too late to go into the OBR forecast and do not change the outlook for productivity growth. He noted that the OBR raised its total factor productivity assumption because of the effect of AI.

squawks.headline: UK mortgage approvals fall to 53.4K in September, below the 54K forecast; M4 money supply grows 0.1% on the month
squawks.detail: Bank of England data put September mortgage approvals at 53.443K against a forecast of 54K, with August revised to 54.814K. M4 money supply rose 0.1% on the month and 3.9% on the year, down from 4.4%, and M4 excluding intermediate OFCs grew at a 1.6% three-month annualised rate, down from 2.8%.

squawks.headline: UK consumer credit rises £1.914bn and mortgage lending £3.866bn, both below forecasts, BoE data show
squawks.detail: Bank of England figures show consumer credit of £1.914bn against a £2bn forecast and £2.464bn previously. Net mortgage lending was £3.866bn against a £4.2bn forecast, with the previous month revised to £4.174bn from £4.410bn.

squawks.headline: UK 10-year gilt yield falls 3bp to 5.29%, a five-week low
squawks.detail: The benchmark 10-year gilt yield fell 3bp to 5.29% in morning trading, its lowest level in five weeks.

squawks.headline: Italian unemployment rate rises to 6.3%, above the 6.2% forecast
squawks.detail: Italy's unemployment rate came in at 6.3%, against a forecast of 6.2% and a previous reading of 6.2%.

squawks.headline: Trump administration is in continuing talks on a temporary peace deal, Semafor reports
squawks.detail: Semafor reports that the US administration is in ongoing talks on a temporary peace deal. The report did not say which conflict the talks cover.

squawks.headline: Iran's Revolutionary Guards navy says three oil tankers hit mines and caught fire south of the Strait of Hormuz
squawks.detail: Iranian reports cite the IRGC navy as saying three tankers caught fire after hitting mines over the past 24 hours while using an unauthorised route off the southern side of the strait. US CENTCOM had earlier rejected Iranian media claims of ships hitting mines and said main transit routes had been cleared.

squawks.headline: Saudi Aramco sets its November butane price at $780 a tonne
squawks.detail: Saudi Aramco has set its contract price for November butane at $780 per tonne, according to a market wire headline.

squawks.headline: EU energy commissioner says the threat to jet fuel supply security seen this summer has passed
squawks.detail: The EU's energy chief said there had been a risk to the security of jet fuel supply this summer and that the risk is no longer present.

squawks.headline: Lloyds Q3 pre-tax profit rises nearly 99% to £2.3bn as costs fall and there are no major impairment charges
squawks.detail: Lloyds Banking Group reported third-quarter pre-tax profit of £2.3bn, ahead of expectations. City AM said the rise came from a lower cost base and the absence of any major impairment charges.

squawks.headline: EU energy commissioner says the bloc uses 18% less gas than in 2022 and is better placed for the current crisis
squawks.detail: The EU energy commissioner said the bloc is better able to handle the current energy crisis than in 2022 because gas use is 18% lower. The commissioner also said the crisis is made worse by its impact on oil products.

squawks.headline: South Korea sets November treasury bond issuance at 12tn won
squawks.detail: South Korea will issue 12tn won of treasury bonds in November. The finance minister had earlier said Seoul would review November issuance in response to market turbulence.

squawks.headline: India's trade minister says the US trade deal will protect farmers and all stakeholders and leave India at a strong comparative advantage
squawks.detail: India's trade minister said that no sensitive interest of farmers or any other stakeholder would be compromised by the planned trade deal with the US. He added that India would hold a strong comparative advantage once the deal is completed.

squawks.headline: Lloyds Q3 net interest income comes in at £3.81bn, just below the £3.83bn estimate
squawks.detail: Lloyds reported Q3 2026 loan-loss provisions of £313.0m (estimate £311.8m) and operating costs of £2.37bn (estimate £2.39bn). Total deposits were £502.8bn, against an estimate of £502.41bn.

squawks.headline: China's commerce ministry says it will take all necessary measures if the EU imposes discriminatory restrictions on Chinese goods
squawks.detail: China's Ministry of Commerce issued the warning about any EU curbs on Chinese products on 29 October. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Healey commits to cutting welfare spending before the next election, with plans due by the end of the year
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that the Chancellor, having delivered her first Budget, has promised to publish plans by the end of the year to reduce a welfare bill she called unsustainable.

squawks.headline: Swedish Q3 GDP rises 0.4% on the quarter, above the 0.3% forecast; September GDP indicator falls 0.7% on the month
squawks.detail: Sweden's Q3 GDP indicator rose 0.4% quarter on quarter, against a 0.3% forecast and 1.4% previously. The monthly indicator for September fell 0.7% after a 1.1% rise, and its annual rate slowed to 2.1% from 3.5%.

squawks.headline: Swedish retail sales fall 0.4% in September and consumer confidence drops to 94.3 in October
squawks.detail: Swedish retail sales fell 0.4% month on month in September after a revised 0.9% rise, and annual growth slowed to 5.5% from a revised 7.2%. Consumer confidence fell to 94.3 in October from 102.2, while manufacturing confidence rose to 111.5 from 106.3.

squawks.headline: Swedish GDP growth slows to 2.8% year on year in advance estimate, just below the 2.9% forecast
squawks.detail: Sweden's advance GDP estimate showed annual growth of 2.8%, against a forecast of 2.9% and down from 3.3% previously.

squawks.headline: China opposes US move to put Chinese firms on a Xinjiang-related entity list and vows to protect its interests
squawks.detail: China's commerce ministry said the US listing of Chinese companies goes against the consensus reached by the two heads of state. It called on Washington to stop immediately and said China will take the steps needed to protect its interests.

squawks.headline: Bank of Korea board member Hwang says it is time to focus on inflation and the won is moving faster than expected
squawks.detail: Hwang said the Bank of Korea is watching the FX market closely and that high borrowing costs are limiting gains for small and medium firms. He cited an upward revision to the 2026 current account surplus to $500bn from $450bn.

squawks.headline: Budget scorecard assumes approval of North Sea discovery drilling producing more than a billion barrels
squawks.detail: City AM reports that the Budget scorecard assumes the government will approve North Sea discovery drilling projects producing over a billion barrels of oil and gas, following Jackdaw and Rosebank.

squawks.headline: US 30-year Treasury yield falls 5bp to 5.311% in Asian trading
squawks.detail: The long bond yield fell 5 basis points to 5.311% during Asian hours on Thursday, while US equity futures sold off.

squawks.headline: China's onshore yuan strengthens to 6.6621 per dollar, its strongest since 7 June 2022
squawks.detail: The onshore yuan rose to 6.6621 per US dollar in Asian trading on Thursday, its strongest level since 7 June 2022.

squawks.headline: RBNZ Governor Breman says the chance of a December rate hike is high
squawks.detail: Reserve Bank of New Zealand Governor Anna Breman said on Thursday that the likelihood of the bank raising the official cash rate in December is high.

squawks.headline: JGB yields rise ahead of the BoJ policy announcement, with the 5-year up 1.5bp at 2.28%
squawks.detail: The 5-year Japanese government bond yield rose 1.5bp to 2.28% as investors waited for the Bank of Japan's policy decision, WSJ reported.

squawks.headline: South Korea's finance minister says Seoul will act promptly on market turbulence and review November bond issuance
squawks.detail: South Korea's finance minister said the government will respond quickly to any jump in market volatility, will carefully assess the size of November treasury bond issuance and will buy back treasury bonds if needed.

squawks.headline: BoC's Macklem says Canada's neutral rate estimate could rise and the inflation forecast assumes fuel costs pass through
squawks.detail: Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem said the estimate of the neutral interest rate may be revised up and the bank's inflation forecast rests on fuel costs passing through to prices. He added that a new model lets the bank break inflation down by component, and described earlier core CPI forecasts as a shortcut.

squawks.headline: Hong Kong Monetary Authority leaves its base rate at 4.25%
squawks.detail: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority kept its base rate unchanged at 4.25% after the Federal Reserve's decision to hold rates.

squawks.headline: Trump says he did not instruct Vance to write to Iran
squawks.detail: President Trump said he had not told Vice President Vance to send the letter to Iran. The WSJ had reported that Vance wrote to a senior Iranian hard-liner to try to restart peace talks.

squawks.headline: Fitch says US fiscal pressures will persist whatever the midterm election result
squawks.detail: Fitch Ratings said pressure on US public finances is set to continue regardless of the outcome of the midterm elections. The post reported no rating action.

squawks.headline: Kremlin aide Ushakov says timing of Abu Dhabi talks on Ukraine depends partly on the battlefield situation
squawks.detail: Kremlin foreign policy aide Yuri Ushakov said the date for the negotiations in Abu Dhabi will depend on factors including the situation on the battlefield and the wider situation. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Budget confirms £1.5bn of devolved loans for mayoral authorities plus extra funding for social housing and rough sleeping
squawks.detail: Inside Housing reports that the Chancellor's Budget repeats the Prime Minister's earlier announcement giving mayoral authorities access to £1.5bn of devolved loans. The Budget also confirms more funding for the Social and Affordable Homes Programme and for rough sleeping.

squawks.headline: Bessent says US trade deals are largely locked in and consumer and business behaviour is strong
squawks.detail: US Treasury Secretary Bessent told CNBC that much of Trump's economic agenda, including tax cuts, is already in place, and that the trade deals are mostly locked in. He also said France has a tough hand. His CNBC appearance has now ended.

squawks.headline: Resolution Foundation says UK plans a much larger fiscal consolidation than other high-income OECD countries
squawks.detail: In its post-Budget analysis, the Resolution Foundation said the government's planned fiscal consolidation is much bigger than those of other high-income OECD countries. It added that it is not yet clear whether the plans will be delivered.

squawks.headline: Global bond sales hit an annual record of $6.61 trillion
squawks.detail: Market reports on 28 October said global bond issuance this year has reached a record $6.61 trillion.

squawks.headline: Bessent says the Iran operation is working and Tehran is cut off from dollars; sees no problem in AI-related borrowing
squawks.detail: In a CNBC interview, US Treasury Secretary Bessent said Operation Outcast on Iran is succeeding, that Iran cannot get dollars and that funding for its proxies is falling. He also said he does not regard AI borrowing or wider spreads on AI-issuer debt as a problem, and described France as having a tough hand.

squawks.headline: Bessent says US faces an energy supply shock and the Fed should keep an open mind; says bonds have done much of the tightening
squawks.detail: US Treasury Secretary Bessent said he expects a strong US third-quarter GDP figure, that the Fed is very attentive to inflation having been above target for a long time, and that yields and oil prices are closely correlated. He also said he and Trump have a lot of confidence in Fed Chair Warsh.

squawks.headline: Trump signs proclamation on US imports of robotics and industrial machinery but imposes no immediate tariffs
squawks.detail: The White House says President Trump has signed a proclamation adjusting US imports of robotics, industrial machinery and their parts and components. It says these imports pose national security risks, but no tariffs take effect immediately.

squawks.headline: Germany will let offshore wind developers hand back auctioned sites if they pay a penalty
squawks.detail: German Economy Minister Katherina Reiche said on Wednesday that companies may return offshore wind sites they won at auction, as long as they pay a penalty to the transmission system operators. Reuters reports that the sector is under growing economic pressure.

squawks.headline: US Vice President Vance writes to a senior Iranian hard-liner in an attempt to restart peace talks, WSJ reports
squawks.detail: The WSJ reports that Vance sent the letter to the secretary of Iran's top security body, a former long-serving IRGC commander. One person said the letter was sent at Trump's direction and that Trump knows about the continuing outreach.

squawks.headline: US proposal reportedly combines Iran's seven conditions with US nuclear demands in phases; Iran wants its conditions met first
squawks.detail: An Al Jazeera reporter says the US proposal pairs Iran's seven conditions with US demands on highly enriched uranium and inspections, to be implemented in phases. The reporter says Iran insists its conditions are met before any nuclear negotiations, while indirect US-Iran messages continue.

squawks.headline: Healey asks BoE to review banks' capital requirements and says the bank tax rise will have a time limit in law
squawks.detail: In post-Budget remarks, Chancellor Healey said she has asked the Bank of England to look at banks' capital requirements and that legislation for the higher bank tax will include a time limit. She also said the government will press ahead with the financial services and markets bill and that business costs were a Budget priority.

squawks.headline: Iran proposal also covers lifting the blockade, the nuclear issue and the return of inspectors, Al Arabiya says
squawks.detail: Al Arabiya reports that the schedule of the new proposal under discussion with Iran covers reopening the Strait of Hormuz, lifting the blockade, dealing with Iran's nuclear programme and calling in inspectors. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: US CENTCOM rejects Iranian media claims that commercial ships are hitting sea mines in the Strait of Hormuz
squawks.detail: US Central Command said claims carried by Iranian-controlled media in recent days and weeks, that commercial vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz were striking sea mines, are false.

squawks.headline: Zelenskiy acknowledges for the first time that Russia needs security guarantees, as US-led peace diplomacy picks up
squawks.detail: The Ukrainian president acknowledged Russia's need for security guarantees, a change in Kyiv's position. He said ending the war and securing Ukraine must still come first.

squawks.headline: US CENTCOM says US forces have cleared sea mines from the main transit routes through the Strait of Hormuz
squawks.detail: US Central Command says all internationally recognised primary transit routes through the Strait of Hormuz have been cleared of sea mines by US forces and remain clear. It says thousands of commercial vessels have used the lanes safely and are still using them today.

squawks.headline: Resolution Foundation says OBR sees UK welfare bill rising by £38bn by 2031-32 while reform waits on reviews
squawks.detail: The Resolution Foundation says the OBR expects welfare spending to increase by £38bn by 2031-32, led by the State Pension and by health and disability benefits for people of working age. It says welfare reform is paused until the Milburn and Timms reviews report.

squawks.headline: Iran and mediators weigh Turkey meeting before 4 November on new proposal covering Hormuz reopening, Al Arabiya says
squawks.detail: Al Arabiya, citing sources, says Iran and mediators are discussing a meeting in Turkey before 4 November. It says the timeline in the new proposal includes reopening the Strait of Hormuz and lifting the siege.

squawks.headline: Warsh ends press conference saying he is comfortable with the Fed tightening financial conditions; Fed not involved in Cook proceedings
squawks.detail: Fed Chair Warsh said tighter financial conditions show that policy is working and that he is not uncomfortable with them. Asked about the proceedings involving Governor Cook, he said the Fed is not involved as far as he knows, and then ended the press conference.

squawks.headline: US 10-year Treasury yield rises 4.11bp to 5.034% during Warsh's press conference
squawks.detail: The 10-year Treasury note yield was last reported up 4.11bp at 5.034% while Fed Chair Warsh was speaking after the Fed's decision to hold rates.

squawks.headline: Warsh says balance sheet task force will report to the FOMC early in Q1 and most Fed colleagues do not see the economy running too hot
squawks.detail: Fed Chair Warsh said any balance sheet changes would follow serious consideration of the task force's recommendations and are unlikely to affect the current policy juncture. He also said productivity has been rising, higher growth does not mean it is causing inflation, and he does not think the Fed has to throw people out of work.

squawks.headline: Warsh says he will not give forward guidance outside a crisis or prejudge December, and that politics played no part in the decision
squawks.detail: At his post-decision press conference, Fed Chair Warsh said the Fed may learn a lot before December and that neither the midterm elections nor politics came up in FOMC deliberations. He also said rates have affected investment inside and outside the technology sector since early September, that capex strength has broadened, that credit spreads have widened for some assets, and that he has noted the rise in oil futures.

squawks.headline: Warsh says the Fed's 2% PCE goal is not a soft target and longer-term inflation expectations remain anchored
squawks.detail: At his post-decision press conference, Fed Chair Warsh said near-term inflation expectations have risen but longer-term measures still show confidence in price stability. He called the FOMC meeting a family fight that reached the right decision, and said market interest rates have turned lower despite a usually stable link with rising oil prices.

squawks.headline: Warsh says swap-based inflation compensation is moving the right way and the Fed removed some accommodation in September
squawks.detail: At his post-decision press conference, Fed Chair Warsh said the period ahead would bring plenty of information and he was comfortable with the signposts. He added that the conclusions of the Fed's five task forces are unlikely to feed into policy at this point, and that he may speak at a task force field hearing on 16 November.

squawks.headline: Fed's Warsh says tightening is starting to work and credit conditions have tightened, but he will not call financial conditions tight
squawks.detail: At his post-decision press conference, Fed Chair Warsh said the Fed removed some accommodation in September, that swap-based inflation compensation is moving the right way and that he is not surprised by market volatility. He said the committee is focused mainly on price stability, will not tolerate inflation above the 2% target, and that the period ahead is rich in information.

squawks.headline: Warsh says the Fed will change its FOMC schedule, with one 2027 meeting lacking a rate vote and 6 policy-setting meetings expected in 2028
squawks.detail: At his press conference, Fed Chair Warsh said the Fed will keep 8 meetings a year, with one focused on strategy and one with no rate vote or statement in 2027, and two without a rate vote in 2028. He also said the Fed has shown it is willing and ready to act, that growth has strengthened and credit conditions have tightened, and that he would not call financial conditions tight.

squawks.headline: WTI December crude settles up 2.88% at $102.78 a barrel
squawks.detail: NYMEX WTI December futures settled $2.88 higher at $102.78 a barrel on Wednesday.

squawks.headline: Fed Chair Warsh says inflation remains elevated and the Fed has not grown easier; sees 3Q US GDP likely above 3%
squawks.detail: At his post-decision press conference, Fed Chair Warsh said economic activity is expanding strongly, business investment is likely rising at a double-digit pace and the committee wants more information to set the policy stance. He said the Fed's responsibility is to get inflation down and that he is not surprised by market volatility.

squawks.headline: IFS says OBR expects 10.8 million higher or additional rate income taxpayers by March 2031
squawks.detail: The IFS says this is 6 million more than if the higher rate threshold had risen with CPI inflation since 2022, and 250,000 more than the OBR forecast in March.

squawks.headline: Canadian 2-year yield reaches a two-year high after the Bank of Canada's rate hike
squawks.detail: Reuters reports Canadian bond yields rose and the Canadian dollar edged higher against the US dollar after the Bank of Canada raised rates for the first time in more than three years.

squawks.headline: Resolution Foundation says global developments since March add £11bn a year on average to OBR underlying borrowing forecast
squawks.detail: The Resolution Foundation says global news since March has raised the OBR's underlying borrowing forecast by £11bn on average across the next five years.

squawks.headline: Arab mediators press Iran for a deal on IAEA inspections and US sanctions relief, Axios says
squawks.detail: Axios reports that Arab mediators are pushing Tehran towards an agreement covering IAEA inspections and relief from US sanctions.

squawks.headline: Traders now price an 80% chance of a December Fed hike
squawks.detail: Market pricing for a December Fed hike stands at 80%, according to a market commentary feed. This follows the Fed's hold earlier today.

squawks.headline: UK to tax sovereign wealth funds on their UK property investments
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports the change will affect countries such as the Gulf states, which are large property investors in Britain.

squawks.headline: Traders keep pricing a 90% chance of a December Fed hike after the hold; short-term rate futures rise
squawks.detail: Short-term US interest rate futures rose after the Fed left rates at 3.75%–4% and traders still price a 90% chance of a December hike. The dollar index fell 0.08% to 102.26 and the euro rose 0.15% to $1.114.

squawks.headline: Axios says possible post-midterm strikes on Iran could target its leadership as the US and Israel coordinate
squawks.detail: Axios cites Israeli and regional sources as saying Iran is under pressure to make nuclear concessions, and that the Israeli military and the US are coordinating ahead of any attacks.

squawks.headline: Fed's Cook and Hammack dissent in favour of a 25bp hike; statement says inflation remains elevated and growth is strong
squawks.detail: The Fed statement says activity is expanding at a strong pace, inflation remains elevated and more information will help determine the policy stance. Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack backed a 25bp hike, and short-term US rate futures were reported rising after the decision.

squawks.headline: Axios reports US and Israel anticipate a week of strikes on Iran after the midterms if nuclear talks fail
squawks.detail: According to Axios, possible strikes would target Iran's leadership, energy and nuclear sites, Iran is being pressed to make nuclear concessions, and the Israeli military and the US are coordinating. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Fed holds rates at 3.75%–4.00% on a 10-2 vote
squawks.detail: The Federal Reserve left its target range for the federal funds rate at 3.75%–4.00%, as expected, with two FOMC members dissenting. The Fed said gathering more information will help it decide the appropriate policy stance.

squawks.headline: HMRC draws up list of 200 billionaires as part of a tax compliance drive on the UK's wealthiest
squawks.detail: The FT reports that HMRC has identified 200 billionaires and is inviting each of them and their representatives to a voluntary early or pre-filing discussion.

squawks.headline: IFS says Budget measures raise the long-run tax take only modestly, much less than the parliament's two earlier Budgets
squawks.detail: The Institute for Fiscal Studies said in its Budget 2026 analysis that the Chancellor's measures produce a modest increase in the long-run tax take, significantly smaller than the increases in the previous two Budgets of this parliament.

squawks.headline: Budget says 10 new English devolution agreements are in their final stages
squawks.detail: A post on the Budget says that, if the 10 agreements are completed, devolution deals would cover over 90% of England's population.

squawks.headline: Long-dated gilt yields fall to a one-month low as Budget borrowing figures match gilt dealers' forecasts
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that the 2026-27 gilt issuance rise of £4.4bn to £250.6bn was close to the £249.6bn Reuters poll. The 2027-28 PSNB forecast of £112bn was in line with the poll.

squawks.headline: Iran's foreign minister says Tehran is still giving diplomacy a chance and is working with intermediaries to speed up its 7-day plan
squawks.detail: Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi said Iran's armed forces are ready to defend the country but Tehran will keep pursuing diplomacy. He said Iran is in ongoing contact with intermediaries over ideas that could put its 7-day plan into effect in less than a week.

squawks.headline: IFS says OBR cuts forecast for household income growth this parliament to 0.4% a year from 0.7%
squawks.detail: The IFS says the OBR's revised forecast would make this the second weakest parliament for household income growth since 1979. It would still beat the last parliament, when disposable incomes fell.

squawks.headline: IFS says OBR sees UK growth slowing markedly next year, with GDP level back to its March path by 2030-31
squawks.detail: The Institute for Fiscal Studies says the OBR puts next year's slowdown down to higher energy prices and interest rates. The OBR expects GDP to fully regain its March-forecast level by 2030-31, with energy prices and inflation forecast to return to pre-war levels.

squawks.headline: Markets price about a 93% chance that the Fed holds rates at 3.75%–4.00% ahead of today's decision
squawks.detail: A market commentator said a hold at 3.75%–4.00% is about 93% priced for the Federal Reserve decision at 2:00pm ET, with Chair Warsh's press conference due at 2:30pm ET.

squawks.headline: US Energy Secretary Wright says Russia can benefit from diesel exports only by ending the war in Ukraine
squawks.detail: The US Energy Secretary tied any Russian gain from diesel exports to an end to the war. He repeated that he expects diesel prices to fall significantly and Gulf diesel exports to rise.

squawks.headline: US Energy Secretary Wright expects diesel prices to fall sharply as Gulf exports rise and China resumes shipments
squawks.detail: US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said diesel exports from the Arabian Gulf are likely to increase and China is likely to resume exporting diesel. He said diesel prices will drop significantly.

squawks.headline: Senior US official says any Iran strike does not depend on Israeli politics and Trump aims to remove threats to Hormuz
squawks.detail: Israel Hayom quotes an unnamed senior US diplomatic official as saying a strike on Iran does not depend on Israel's political process. The official also says Trump is still determined to fully neutralise Iran's military nuclear programme and remove military threats to the Strait of Hormuz and to Iran's neighbours.

squawks.headline: Resolution Foundation says OBR forecasts put 2020s income growth as the weakest of any decade on record
squawks.detail: The Resolution Foundation said the OBR's latest forecasts show incomes ending the decade only 1.4% higher in 2030 than in 2020.

squawks.headline: Meloni says Italy's 2027 budget includes €26bn of tax cuts and spending increases
squawks.detail: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said the 2027 budget contains tax cuts and spending increases worth €26bn.

squawks.headline: Budget documents show mayors' share of income tax will cover basic-rate receipts only
squawks.detail: Government Budget documents show that the devolved income tax share for mayors will be limited to basic-rate revenues, an economist noted. Higher and additional rate receipts are not included.

squawks.headline: US crude futures rise $3 a barrel as fighting in Yemen raises Middle East supply concerns
squawks.detail: A market newswire reports US crude prices up $3 a barrel. The move is attributed to concerns over Middle East supply after fighting in Yemen.

squawks.headline: Healey says the main UK minimum wage rate will rise by 3.9%
squawks.detail: Chancellor John Healey announced on Wednesday that the main minimum wage rate will increase by 3.9%, Reuters reports.

squawks.headline: Budget's cost of living package centres on a £100 council tax rebate for Band A–D homes to help with winter energy bills
squawks.detail: According to the Resolution Foundation, the main measure in the Chancellor's cost of living package is a £100 council tax rebate for households in Bands A to D, aimed at rising energy bills this winter.

squawks.headline: IFS says current budget surplus by 2029-30 is still on track but smaller, with day-to-day borrowing likely in 2028-29
squawks.detail: The Institute for Fiscal Studies says the government remains on track for a current budget surplus by 2029-30, but a smaller one, with more of the fall in borrowing coming in later years. It says the government is now likely to be borrowing for day-to-day spending in 2028-29.

squawks.headline: UK markets react calmly to Healey's first Budget after pledge to keep to borrowing rules
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that UK markets took the chancellor's first Budget calmly on Wednesday. Investors drew comfort from the government's commitment to stick to its borrowing rules.

squawks.headline: Mexico's Sheinbaum says US trade deal talks continue and Mexico is weighing whether a deal before the midterms is possible
squawks.detail: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum said talks with the US on a trade deal are continuing. Mexico is assessing whether an agreement can be reached before the US midterm elections.

squawks.headline: BoC's Rogers says the Bank does not see a Middle East resolution as imminent
squawks.detail: Bank of Canada Senior Deputy Governor Rogers made the remark at the press conference following the Bank's 25bp rate rise to 2.5%. The press conference has now ended.

squawks.headline: Zelenskiy says the energy ceasefire is not holding and Ukraine is hitting Russian energy sites in response to attacks
squawks.detail: Ukraine's President Zelenskiy said the energy ceasefire is not working. He said Ukraine now responds to Russian attacks on its energy infrastructure by striking Russian energy infrastructure.

squawks.headline: Dutch PM says no European ally is willing to buy Russian energy
squawks.detail: The Dutch prime minister said no European ally is prepared to buy Russian energy and described doing so as a foolish decision.

squawks.headline: BoC's Rogers says policymakers broadly agreed inflation risks had risen and discussed both holding and raising rates
squawks.detail: Bank of Canada Senior Deputy Governor Carolyn Rogers said there was strong consensus that inflation risks were rising. She said the Governing Council discussed whether to hold or raise rates, which she called common practice.

squawks.headline: Zelenskiy expects clarity on peace talks after the US elections and will discuss territory only at leaders' level
squawks.detail: Ukraine's President Zelenskiy said he expects clarity on talks with Russia and the US after the US elections. He said territory would only be discussed at leaders' level and called for European unity to help end the war.

squawks.headline: Zelenskiy hopes for Ukraine-US-Russia talks between 6 and 10 November and no later than end-November
squawks.detail: Ukraine's President Zelenskiy said Kyiv hopes the trilateral talks with the US and Russia will take place between 6 and 10 November, and that they should happen no later than the end of November.

squawks.headline: Budget commits to ringfencing preventative spending at the 2027 Spending Review
squawks.detail: The Institute for Government reported that the Chancellor will ringfence preventative spending at the 2027 Spending Review, a Budget measure the IfG had argued for.

squawks.headline: Macklem says US trade and Middle East uncertainty could change the BoC outlook; Rogers calls housing forecast subdued
squawks.detail: Speaking after the rate decision, Bank of Canada Governor Macklem said uncertainty over US trade and the Middle East could alter the outlook. Senior Deputy Governor Rogers said uncertainty over the economy and borrowing rates is weighing on housing, and called the bank's housing forecast subdued.

squawks.headline: Macklem says the Bank of Canada has no set path for rates and inflation now looks less likely to stay well contained
squawks.detail: Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem said after the 25bp hike that raising rates will limit how far higher oil prices pass through, and that businesses are planning to pass on high input costs. He also said changing direction is always a difficult decision.

squawks.headline: Macklem says the Bank of Canada's policy rate is still low enough not to restrain growth, even after the hike
squawks.detail: At his press conference after the rate rise, Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem said hiking will limit how much higher oil prices pass through to inflation. He also said investment in the energy sector is rising and investment estimates may be conservative.

squawks.headline: Healey makes online marketplaces responsible for collecting VAT owed by sellers on their platforms
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that the Chancellor said on Wednesday that online marketplaces will have to collect the VAT owed by retailers who sell through them.

squawks.headline: Foreign banks are not exempt from the higher UK bank surcharge
squawks.detail: A market commentary account reports that foreign firms get no exemption from the higher bank surcharge announced in the Budget.

squawks.headline: OBR forecasts real household disposable income per person still more than ¾% below its March path in 2030-31
squawks.detail: The Resolution Foundation, reading the Budget documents, says the OBR has real household disposable income falling this year and real earnings growth at zero in 2027 and 2028. The Guardian reports the living standards outlook was downgraded partly because of the Middle East conflict.

squawks.headline: OBR says the welfare cap will be missed by £2.8bn, putting the government technically in breach of one fiscal rule
squawks.detail: The OBR's Budget documents show social security spending on course to exceed the welfare cap by £2.8bn, a technical breach of that rule.

squawks.headline: ADNOC tells clients its new pipeline bypassing the Strait of Hormuz will start in early 2027
squawks.detail: Abu Dhabi's national oil company has told clients that its new pipeline route avoiding the Strait of Hormuz is due to begin operating in early 2027, according to a market commentary account. The post did not report any price reaction.

squawks.headline: UK plans reform of electricity standing charges, Treasury Budget documents show
squawks.detail: Treasury documents published with the Budget say the government will reform electricity standing charges. No further details were given in the report.

squawks.headline: Government says England's regions will keep a share of locally raised income tax and business rates
squawks.detail: Reuters reports the government's fiscal devolution plan, published on Wednesday alongside the Budget, will let England's regions retain part of the income tax and business rates raised in their areas.

squawks.headline: Gilts extend rally as UK 30-year yield drops 5bp to a day low of 5.70%
squawks.detail: Market wire reports UK gilts extending gains during the Budget, with the 30-year yield down 5bp at an intraday low of 5.70%.

squawks.headline: DMO expects to price Treasury bill repo facility 20bp below Bank Rate and sets up £250mn collateral pool per bill
squawks.detail: The DMO said its Treasury bill standing repo facility is likely to be priced at 20bp below BoE Bank Rate, subject to review. It is also introducing a collateral pool holding £250mn of each Treasury bill.

squawks.headline: DMO says its standing repo facility for Treasury bills will start in January
squawks.detail: The UK Debt Management Office says a standing repo facility covering Treasury bills will begin operating in January.

squawks.headline: OBR puts UK headroom before Budget measures at £12.5bn in 2029-30
squawks.detail: The OBR estimates fiscal headroom in 2029-30 at £12.5bn before the Budget measures are taken into account.

squawks.headline: Losses on the BoE's quantitative tightening for 2027-28 are put at £5.7bn more than forecast in March
squawks.detail: The higher estimate of losses on the Bank of England's QT programme for 2027-28 was reported on Budget day. It is £5.7bn above the March forecast.

squawks.headline: Kremlin says Europeans will not join the trilateral Ukraine talks and a date will be announced soon
squawks.detail: Kremlin aide Ushakov said European representatives are not being invited to the negotiations on Ukraine, Interfax reported. The Kremlin also said the date of the trilateral talks would be announced soon.

squawks.headline: Bank of Canada signals further hikes may be needed and raises its inflation forecasts to 2.9% for 2026 and 3.1% for 2027
squawks.detail: The Bank of Canada's Monetary Policy Report now puts inflation at 2.9% in 2026 (2.5% in July), 3.1% in 2027 (2.0%) and 2.2% in 2028 (2.1%), above target until mid-2028. It assumes Brent averages around $100 in Q4 before easing to around $75 by end-2028. Governor Macklem said the hike was meant to stop high energy prices spreading into wider inflation, that rates may have to rise again and that the council will go carefully, deciding one meeting at a time.

squawks.headline: OBR says the government's council housebuilding ambition could cost an extra £3bn-£4bn a year
squawks.detail: The Office for Budget Responsibility put this estimate on the council housebuilding plans in its Budget documents.

squawks.headline: OBR expects the Employment Rights Act to have a negative economic impact
squawks.detail: The Office for Budget Responsibility gave this assessment of the Employment Rights Act alongside the Budget. No figures were reported.

squawks.headline: Bank of Canada raises its key rate by 25bp to 2.5%, in line with forecasts
squawks.detail: The Bank of Canada lifted its key rate to 2.5% from 2.25%, matching the 2.5% forecast. It is the bank's first rate rise in three years.

squawks.headline: UK plans to extend its forthcoming carbon border tax to refined products, Treasury documents show
squawks.detail: Treasury Budget documents show the government plans to widen the scope of its upcoming carbon border tax to cover refined products.

squawks.headline: OBR says headroom would be £10.2bn if fuel duty stayed frozen; cumulative cost of freezes and 5p cut reaches £139bn
squawks.detail: The OBR's Budget documents put headroom at £10.2bn if fuel duty had stayed frozen. It also says the cumulative cost of fuel duty freezes and the 5p cut has risen to £139bn.

squawks.headline: OBR puts the chance of meeting the fiscal mandate at 56%, down from 59% at Budget 2025
squawks.detail: The OBR also says the Budget plans slow the near-term pace of fiscal consolidation compared with the previous plans.

squawks.headline: OBR expects the UK tax-to-GDP ratio to pass its 37.2% record in 2027-28 and keep rising
squawks.detail: The OBR says the ratio rises in every year of the forecast. It also expects the bank tax increase to bring in £1bn in receipts in 2027-28.

squawks.headline: OBR raises 2026-27 UK borrowing forecast to £133.2bn from £115.5bn, and 2027-28 to £112bn from £96.5bn
squawks.detail: The OBR's Budget forecast puts government borrowing at £68.3bn in 2031-32. Net borrowing over 2026-31 is reported as £65bn higher than in the previous forecast.

squawks.headline: European benchmark gas price hits €100/MWh, its first time at that level since December 2022
squawks.detail: The European benchmark gas price is reported reaching €100/MWh, a level last seen during the 2022 energy crisis.

squawks.headline: OBR expects UK CPI inflation to peak at 3.75% on a quarterly basis in early 2027
squawks.detail: The quarterly peak is in the OBR's central forecast, published alongside the Budget.

squawks.headline: OBR cuts headroom against the debt rule to £24bn from £27.1bn
squawks.detail: The OBR says Budget policies add £3.5bn to borrowing in 2027-28 and cut it by £11.7bn in 2031-32. Reported calculations show £65bn more borrowing over 2026-27 to 2030-31 than in the March forecast.

squawks.headline: OBR raises UK inflation forecast to 3.1% for 2026 and 3.5% for 2027
squawks.detail: The OBR's Economic and Fiscal Outlook puts 2026 inflation at 3.1%, up from 2.3%, and 2027 inflation at 3.5% in its central forecast, up from 2% in March.

squawks.headline: OBR calls fiscal margins very small and says a 1% rate move shifts debt interest by £16bn
squawks.detail: The OBR describes the UK fiscal position as very challenging and says a higher, longer energy price peak could lift 2027-28 borrowing £17bn above its central forecast. It adds that productivity growth 0.5 percentage points higher or lower could leave borrowing £50bn lower or £40bn higher.

squawks.headline: DMO cuts long conventional syndication to £12.5bn and raises index-linked syndication to £7.8bn for 2026-27
squawks.detail: The revised DMO remit sets long-dated conventional gilt syndications at £12.5bn, down from £15bn in April. Index-linked syndications rise to £7.8bn from £7bn, and index-linked auctions fall to £15.6bn from £16bn.

squawks.headline: World Bank forecasts global energy prices up 32% in 2026, a four-year high, on Middle East war
squawks.detail: The World Bank expects global oil supply to fall 5.2% in 2026 and overall commodity prices to rise 23% before falling 7% in 2027. It warns that further Middle East escalation or damage to Russian oil infrastructure could lift energy prices further.

squawks.headline: DMO sets 2026-27 gross gilt issuance at £250.6bn, above the £249.6bn poll and the April remit of £246.2bn
squawks.detail: The UK Debt Management Office published its revised 2026-27 financing remit alongside the Budget. Planned gross gilt issuance is £250.6bn, compared with £249.6bn expected in a poll and £246.2bn in the April remit.

squawks.headline: Healey takes total government backing for council homes to £40bn and makes land sold to social housing providers VAT-free
squawks.detail: In the Budget, Chancellor Healey also announced £1.5bn for a social and affordable housing programme. He said all land sold to social housing providers will be free of VAT.

squawks.headline: Healey sets a target of 3% of GDP for UK defence spending in 2030
squawks.detail: Chancellor Healey gave the target for UK defence spending during his Budget speech.

squawks.headline: Healey replaces the lifetime ISA with a first-time buyer ISA and gives £4.7bn to a 'Your first home' scheme
squawks.detail: Chancellor Healey announced both measures in his Budget speech.

squawks.headline: Canadian official says trade talks with the US have made limited progress
squawks.detail: Reuters cited a Canadian government official familiar with the talks, speaking on Wednesday.

squawks.headline: Budget sets up a defence finance taskforce, with the National Wealth Fund and National Bank deploying up to £5bn on defence
squawks.detail: Healey said the government will start treaty talks with Finland, Poland and the Netherlands on a multilateral defence mechanism and will set out how it meets its NATO defence commitment. The National Wealth Fund and the National Bank will put up to £5bn of funding and investment into the defence industrial base.

squawks.headline: Healey commits £10bn more in support for Ukraine in the Budget
squawks.detail: In his Budget speech, Chancellor Healey announced a further £10bn of support for Ukraine and said Britain would back Ukraine for as long as needed.

squawks.headline: Healey says triple lock changes save £50bn by 2050, with a pensions double lock saving £15bn
squawks.detail: In his Budget speech, Chancellor Healey said changes to the state pension triple lock will save £50bn by 2050. He also said a double lock on pensions will save £15bn.

squawks.headline: Healey says the Budget fully funds the defence investment plan
squawks.detail: In his Budget speech, Chancellor Healey said the government will fully fund the defence investment plan. No figures were given in the reports.

squawks.headline: Healey says local authorities will keep 100% of business rates by the end of the decade as he moves to devolve tax revenues
squawks.detail: In his Budget statement, Chancellor Healey said the government is taking steps to devolve tax revenues. He said local authorities will retain all business rates by the end of the decade.

squawks.headline: Budget creates a new Good Growth Fund for local mayors
squawks.detail: Chancellor Healey announced a new Good Growth Fund for local mayors in the Budget. No funding figure was given in the reports.

squawks.headline: Healey announces a founders relief within capital gains tax in the Budget
squawks.detail: Chancellor Healey announced a new founders relief in capital gains tax during the Budget speech. No further details were given in the reports.

squawks.headline: Budget sets out £140mn investment in strategic British AI companies
squawks.detail: The UK Budget includes £140mn of investment for strategic British AI firms, as announced during Chancellor Healey's speech.

squawks.headline: Healey allocates £20.4bn to the National Wealth Fund in the Budget
squawks.detail: Chancellor Healey announced £20.4bn for the National Wealth Fund in his Budget speech. He also announced a new British data centre covenant but gave no figures for it.

squawks.headline: Budget lifts the bank surcharge to 6% from 3% for 15 months starting in January
squawks.detail: In the Budget, Chancellor Healey's 3 percentage point increase takes the bank surcharge to 6% from 3%. The extra charge applies for 15 months from January.

squawks.headline: Budget adds 3% to the bank surcharge
squawks.detail: Chancellor Healey told parliament in the Budget that banks will pay an extra 3% on the bank surcharge.

squawks.headline: Healey raises tax rates on income from property and savings by 2 percentage points in the Budget
squawks.detail: In the Budget speech, Chancellor Healey announced higher tax rates on property and savings income, with the increase reported as 2 percentage points. He also said the threshold for business asset disposal relief is being cut.

squawks.headline: Healey drops the planned cash ISA change and keeps the £20k cash ISA limit for all ages
squawks.detail: In the Budget, Chancellor Healey said the planned change to cash ISAs will not go ahead and the cash ISA limit stays at £20k for people of all ages.

squawks.headline: Zelenskiy says Ukraine-Russia-US talks could take place as early as 10 November
squawks.detail: Ukrainian reports cite President Zelenskiy as saying that three-way negotiations between Ukraine, Russia and the United States could start as early as 10 November.

squawks.headline: Budget lifts duty on gaming machines to 25% from 20% as Healey raises gambling taxes
squawks.detail: Chancellor Healey announced higher gambling taxes in the Budget, including a rise in gaming machine duty to 25% from 20%. He also announced tighter rules on online marketplaces so that sellers cannot avoid paying VAT.

squawks.headline: Budget extends the 5p fuel duty cut to July 2027 and suspends tariffs on more than 100 supermarket products
squawks.detail: Chancellor Healey announced in the Budget that the 5p cut in fuel duty is extended to July 2027. He also announced that tariffs on more than 100 supermarket products are being suspended.

squawks.headline: OBR raises its 2027-28 UK borrowing forecast to 3.4% of GDP from 2.9%
squawks.detail: The OBR's Budget forecast raises borrowing for 2027-28 to 3.4% of GDP from 2.9%. It also has the deficit falling to 1.8% of GDP by 2031-32.

squawks.headline: OBR forecasts UK net financial debt at 83.1% of GDP in 2029-30, easing to 82.3% by 2030-31
squawks.detail: Budget forecasts put UK net financial debt at 83.1% of GDP in 2029-30. The OBR projects the ratio easing to 82.3% by 2030-31.

squawks.headline: Healey raises the national living wage by 3.9% in the Budget
squawks.detail: Chancellor Rachel Healey announced a 3.9% rise in the national living wage in his Budget statement.

squawks.headline: Healey exempts pensioners with income up to the full state pension from income tax under a new pension allowance
squawks.detail: Chancellor Healey announced a new pension tax allowance in the Budget. Under it, pensioners whose income is no higher than the new full state pension will not pay income tax.

squawks.headline: Healey announces £100 energy payment for 20mn households at a cost of £2.6bn and extends electricity VAT cut to July 2027
squawks.detail: In the Budget speech, Chancellor Healey said 20 million households will receive a £100 energy payment, at a cost of £2.6bn. He also extended the VAT cut on electricity bills to July 2027.

squawks.headline: Budget says £1 in every £13 of government spending goes on debt interest
squawks.detail: The government's Budget statement put debt interest at £1 in every £13 of public spending.

squawks.headline: Healey scraps the planned gas shippers obligation and moves more older renewables onto fixed-price contracts
squawks.detail: In the Budget, Chancellor Healey set out a new cost-controlled framework for energy bills, saying it aims to bring UK energy costs into line with Europe and reduce the effect of international gas prices on bills. He also said the UK remains committed to net zero by 2050.

squawks.headline: OBR cuts its 2027 UK GDP growth forecast to 1% from 1.6%
squawks.detail: The Budget forecasts cut UK GDP growth for 2027 to 1% from 1.6%, while 2026 growth was raised to 1.2% from 1.1%.

squawks.headline: OBR raises its 2026 UK GDP growth forecast to 1.2% from 1.1% in March
squawks.detail: Chancellor Healey gave the upgraded OBR growth forecast in his Budget speech.

squawks.headline: Healey says fiscal headroom rises from £15bn to £22bn by 2030-31, with the rules met in the third forecast year
squawks.detail: The OBR's £15bn headroom against the current budget rule is down from £23.6bn in March and in line with the £15bn poll. The Chancellor said it climbs to £22bn by 2030-31 and that the fiscal rules will be met in the third year of the forecast.

squawks.headline: Healey rules out broad tax rises and cuts to public services in the Budget
squawks.detail: The Chancellor told Parliament his Budget aims to give families and businesses breathing space. He also said he will start a radical reform of energy to bring bills down.

squawks.headline: OBR forecasts UK borrowing at 4.2% of GDP in 2026-27, up from 3.6% previously, falling to 1.8% by 2031-32
squawks.detail: Chancellor Healey set out the OBR's Budget forecasts. They put public sector net financial liabilities at 83.2% of GDP in 2026-27, against 82.6% in March, and net financial debt at 82.3% of GDP in 2030-31.

squawks.headline: UK Budget puts fiscal headroom against the spending rule at £15bn, slightly below the £15.2bn expected
squawks.detail: The headroom figure was reported as Chancellor Healey presented the Budget on 28 October. It compares with an expected £15.2bn.

squawks.headline: Healey says he meets the fiscal rules and will use some headroom to absorb the Iran war, with debt interest up £14bn this year
squawks.detail: In his Budget speech, the Chancellor said he would keep cutting borrowing, would not raise tax on working people and had rejected broad-based tax rises. He said the OBR names the Middle East war as a key driver of its forecasts and that debt interest spending is £14bn higher this year.

squawks.headline: US preliminary wholesale inventories rise 0.6% m/m in September, above the 0.5% forecast
squawks.detail: US wholesale inventories rose 0.6% m/m in the preliminary September reading, against a forecast and a previous reading of 0.5%. Advance retail inventories excluding autos rose 0.4%, after 0.0% the month before.

squawks.headline: Healey opens Budget speech saying it rests on fiscal discipline and backs British business for growth
squawks.detail: As he opened the Budget statement, Chancellor Healey said the Budget was for working people, would be built on fiscal discipline and would back British enterprise to drive growth. These were his opening remarks to the Commons.

squawks.headline: US advance goods trade deficit widens to $134.9bn, more than the $130.2bn forecast
squawks.detail: The advance US goods trade balance came in at -$134.9bn, against a forecast of -$130.2bn and -$132.07bn previously. In the same release, advance wholesale inventories rose 0.6% m/m, against a forecast of 0.5% and 0.5% previously.

squawks.headline: PM Burnham pledges to do all he can to secure a better EU deal for the UK
squawks.detail: Prime Minister Burnham said he would do everything he could to obtain an improved deal with the EU for the UK.

squawks.headline: Chancellor Healey begins presenting the UK Budget
squawks.detail: Reuters is carrying a live broadcast of Chancellor John Healey presenting the Budget on 28 October.

squawks.headline: US secured overnight financing rate rises to 3.95% on 27 October from 3.93%
squawks.detail: The US secured overnight financing rate was 3.95% on 27 October, compared with 3.93% on 26 October.

squawks.headline: Gulf stocks fall after an attack on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery revives fears of Middle East escalation
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that Gulf equity markets fell in early trade on Wednesday after an attack on the Ras Tanura refinery in Saudi Arabia, the largest crude exporter. The attack revived concerns that the conflict in the Middle East could escalate.

squawks.headline: Healey's Budget bank tax rise is reported to be temporary, with the surcharge set below 8%
squawks.detail: Reports ahead of Chancellor Healey's Budget say the higher tax on banks will be temporary and the bank surcharge will come in under 8%.

squawks.headline: Bank of Canada is widely expected to raise its key rate by 25bp to 2.5% on Wednesday, its first hike in three years
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that most economists expect the Bank of Canada to raise its benchmark rate by 25bp to 2.5% on Wednesday. Economists see the move as protection against energy inflation spreading more widely.

squawks.headline: US regulator proposes rules to speed up LNG projects and expand export capacity
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that a US regulator on Wednesday proposed new rules to speed up liquefied natural gas projects and expand export capacity. The proposal is part of the Trump administration's wider push on energy infrastructure.

squawks.headline: Germany's 10-year Bund auction averages 3.37%, down from 3.58% last time; bid-to-cover falls to 1.1
squawks.detail: The average yield at Germany's 10-year Bund auction was 3.37%, compared with 3.58% at the previous sale. The bid-to-cover ratio was 1.1, down from 1.2.

squawks.headline: Russia's Novak denies that Moscow is in talks with the US about American companies returning to Russian oil projects
squawks.detail: Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said Russia is not negotiating with the US on a return to oil projects, TASS reported. This follows FT reports that the US was discussing Russian deals for American oil majors as part of the Ukraine peace talks.

squawks.headline: Zelenskiy says Russia could also get security guarantees as part of a Ukraine peace deal, FT reports
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that Ukraine's president has acknowledged Moscow could receive security guarantees under a peace settlement. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Senior Iranian official denies Qatar has made a new proposal to end hostilities with the US and calls its ideas unacceptable
squawks.detail: A senior Iranian official said Qatar had not presented a fresh plan to end hostilities with the US, and that the ideas Qatar had put forward were unacceptable to Tehran. The official added that Iran's refusal to show flexibility on the nuclear issue is unchanged.

squawks.headline: Iran's president says the government is working to end the state of 'neither war nor peace'
squawks.detail: Iran's President Pezeshkian said the government is working to get beyond the current state of neither war nor peace. Qatari mediators have given Iran a new draft deal, and Iran is expected to respond by the end of the week.

squawks.headline: Italian producer prices rise 3.6% m/m in September
squawks.detail: Italian producer prices rose 3.6% month on month in September, according to the data release.

squawks.headline: China's commerce minister notes recent EU trade restrictions on China and calls the EU an important trade partner
squawks.detail: China's commerce minister said in a statement that China has taken note of recent EU restrictive trade measures against it, and described China and the EU as important economic and trade partners.

squawks.headline: Healey's Budget is set to focus on the cost of living, with modest measures and major decisions put off, Guardian reports
squawks.detail: The Guardian reports that Chancellor Healey will frame today's Budget around the cost of living crisis at what he calls a difficult moment. It says only modest policies are expected and that important decisions will be deferred.

squawks.headline: Qatari mediators give Iran a new draft deal with a seven-day timeline; Iran's response is expected by the end of the week
squawks.detail: An official briefed on the negotiations says Qatari mediators handed Iran the draft in Tehran on Sunday. Under the draft, both sides would take confidence-building steps every day, several countries would act as guarantors, and the timeline could begin early next week.

squawks.headline: China urges Germany and the EU to take a rational approach on trade and supply chains
squawks.detail: China's foreign ministry said on Wednesday that it is committed to keeping global industrial and supply chains stable and secure. It was responding to German Chancellor Merz's proposal for wider EU-Asia market access to counter trade restrictions.

squawks.headline: China says it will pay consumption subsidies faster to support spending
squawks.detail: China announced on 28 October that it will speed up subsidy payments aimed at lifting consumption. The report gave no amounts or timetable.

squawks.headline: Russia's Ryabkov says Moscow is preparing for Ukraine negotiations and hopes US dialogue can address the conflict's root causes
squawks.detail: Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov said Russia is in the preparation phase for negotiations on Ukraine. He also said Moscow hopes close dialogue with the US administration will help resolve the root causes of the conflict.

squawks.headline: Zelenskiy says Ukraine will not target Russian ships carrying diesel bound for the US
squawks.detail: Ukraine's President Zelenskiy said Ukraine would not attack Russian vessels transporting diesel to the United States. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Brent and US crude futures rise more than $2 as supply risks return
squawks.detail: Brent and US crude futures were reported up by more than $2 a barrel, with the rise put down to renewed supply risks.

squawks.headline: German GfK consumer sentiment weakens to -30.8, below the -30.3 forecast
squawks.detail: The GfK consumer sentiment index for Germany came in at -30.8, compared with a forecast of -30.3 and -30.6 previously.

squawks.headline: Chancellor Healey abolishes standing charges on household gas bills
squawks.detail: A market news account reports that the UK Chancellor is scrapping standing charges on gas bills and presents the change as making payments fairer. The report comes ahead of Wednesday's Budget.

squawks.headline: Bank of England is set to begin short-term precautionary monetary tightening in November, FT reports
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that the Bank of England plans to start short-term precautionary tightening at its November meeting. The report came out before the UK Budget.

squawks.headline: Trump leaves open the possibility of further attacks on Iran after the election
squawks.detail: President Trump said he would not rule out more strikes on Iran once the US election is over.

squawks.headline: Trump says Ukraine peace efforts are progressing and he hopes to hold talks with Putin and Zelenskiy soon
squawks.detail: President Trump said efforts on Ukraine are moving forward and that he hopes to meet both Putin and Zelenskiy in the near future.

squawks.headline: Japan's 2-year government bond yield rises 2bp to 1.895%
squawks.detail: The 2-year JGB yield climbed 2bp to 1.895%, while the 5-year yield rose 3.5bp to 2.265%.

squawks.headline: Sterling edges lower towards $1.3300 ahead of the Budget and the Fed decision
squawks.detail: GBP/USD drifted towards 1.3300 in Asian trading, ahead of Chancellor Healey's Budget and the Federal Reserve rate decision, according to an FX market report.
